title: Cycle Tranche Staffing and Scope Trimming Guidelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: provide a compact, operational set of rules and templates for dividing a product cycle into time-boxed tranches, allocating headcount across core vs. surge lanes, and making defensible scope cuts in the final two weeks. This doc codifies a repeatable process so PMs and Eng leads can make consistent tradeoffs under pressure with minimal coordination overhead.

Core ideas: divide each 3-week cycle into three tranches (Foundations, Feature Run, Stabilize). Reserve a small float pool (~10-15% of committed FTEs) for unplanned bugs, infra work, and early customer escalations. Define explicit cut gates at T-10d and T-3d where features are either green/amber/red. Use a cross-functional Scope Tribunal (PM, Eng Lead, Design Lead, QA Lead) to adjudicate amber/red items using the triage matrix below.

Roles & responsibilities: PM - maintain tranche backlog and priority signals; Eng Lead - capacity commitments, identify blockers; Design Lead - scope reduction options that preserve UX integrity; QA Lead - test coverage and release risk score. EMs own final sprint allocations and agreement with PMs on deferred work.

Tranche definitions: Foundations (days 0-5): infra, long-lead items, schema changes, model onboarding prep. Feature Run (days 6-14): primary roadmap work; aim for 70% of planned story points. Stabilize (days 15-21): regression fixes, bake time, safety checks, performance tuning, rollout playbooks.

Staffing model: commit using FTE-equivalents (1 FTE = 16 points per cycle baseline). For each squad, compute: Planned FTE = committed points / 16. Float Pool = round_up(sum(Planned FTEs) * 0.12). Designate 1-2 engineers as surge champions for cross-team triage. For Dedicated and Private product work (high infra risk) increase float pool to 18%.

Cut gates and decision rules: T-10d triage: any feature failing >2 acceptance criteria or missing >30% of implementation tasks becomes Amber. T-3d freeze: Amber features must be either reduced to a known-safe subset (trimmed) or moved to backlog. Red features (security/regulatory blockers, major stability regressions) are pulled immediately. Prioritization order for cuts: compliance/security -> customer-SLO hotspots -> platform integrity -> new UX polish.

Triage matrix (qualitative guidance):
- Customer impact: High / Medium / Low
- Implementation delta: Large / Medium / Small
- Testability: Blocked / Partial / Covered
- Rollout risk: High / Medium / Low
Use scoring: High impact + Small delta + Covered tests = keep; Low impact + Large delta = cut.

Operational checklist (pre-cycle):
- PMs publish tranche-aligned backlog with clear MRs and acceptance criteria. (Confluence: /CycleOps/Tranche-Templates)
- Eng Leads upload draft capacity numbers to CycleOps spreadsheet and tag surge candidates.
- Design owners upload trimmed UX options (3-tier: full / mini / stub).

Operational checklist (during):
- T-10d triage meeting scheduled with stakeholders and a recorded decision in ticket.
- T-3d freeze announcement: no new features are accepted; only defined stabilizations allowed.
- Final 48h runway: ship-blocking fixes only; scope tribunal meets if disagreements arise.

Cut templates (examples to use in tickets):
- Trim to MVP: list the 2 minimal endpoints or screens required; defer remaining flows.
- Replace with guardrail: ship a feature flag and limited rollout for risky integrations.
- Defer non-essential telemetry: postpone enhanced metrics collection to next cycle.

Metrics to track post-cycle: percent of committed points delivered, percent of scope trimmed, number of emergency rollbacks, cycle defect rate, customer-facing incidents. Target thresholds: deliver >= 85% committed points; trimmed <= 15% of planned scope.

2026-02-20: Received feedback from Eng Leads - requested clearer FTE conversion and dedicated surge champion guidelines.
2026-02-25: Updated float pool guidance to 12% baseline and 18% for infra-heavy tracks per ENG input.
2026-03-03: Run mock triage during PM sync; Design proposed 3-tier trimmed UX template and QA added a release-risk scorecard.
2026-03-08: Sent to Heads of Product and Eng for review. Requested sign-off from Legal for regulatory gating language.

acceptance_criteria: A tranche template created in Confluence and linked from the PM handbook
CycleOps spreadsheet includes FTE calculations and float pool auto-calculations
One pilot team runs the T-10d and T-3d gates with recorded decisions
Post-cycle metrics captured and compared to target thresholds
risks: Teams may under-estimate integration work leading to larger-than-expected carryover
Overly aggressive trimming could degrade UX if Design trim options are not high quality
Float pool used for long-running infra work reduces surge capacity for urgent customer fixes
notes: Suggestion from Eng review: add a 'rollback rehearsal' in Stabilize tranche for complex model rollouts.
PM lead to run a 30-minute onboarding session for PMs and EMs before pilot cycle starts.
If pilot shows >20% trimmed scope, we'll iterate on velocity assumptions and float pool sizing.
